# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Mute. I hold the manual, which states that any text printed on the bomb is a trap ("bait"). The only valid defusal method relies on an external light source indicating which wire to cut: Blue light means Cut Green wire; Red light means Cut Yellow wire; Yellow light means Cut Red wire.

Deaf can see my gestures and the bomb. Blind can touch the bomb but cannot see or hear. Deaf must physically guide Blind's hands to the correct wire based on the light color observed. Since Deaf does not know the mapping rules (which are in the manual I hold), I must transmit these rules via gesture.

To do this, we need a shared code for colors. I will propose the following arbitrary but distinct mappings using the allowed gesture alphabet:
- **Blue**: 🤟 (Shaka sign, often associated with ocean/relaxation)
- **Green**: 👍 (Thumbs up, "Go")
- **Red**: ✋ (Stop hand, "Stop/Danger")
- **Yellow**: 🤘 (Rock on sign, distinct from others)

The logic is: If Light Color X, then Cut Wire Color Y.
1. Blue Light -> Cut Green Wire: Sequence `🤟` (Light) `👍` (Wire) `🤝` (Link/Action).
2. Red Light -> Cut Yellow Wire: Sequence `✋` (Light) `🤘` (Wire) `🤝` (Link/Action).
3. Yellow Light -> Cut Red Wire: Sequence `🤘` (Light) `✋` (Wire) `🤝` (Link/Action).

I also need to emphasize ignoring the text. Text is represented by ✍. Ignoring it is 👎. So `✍ 👎`.

I will send these sequences to Deaf so they can interpret the bomb's state and act accordingly.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🤘", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤘", "✋", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Does the manual allow pushing the button?
Deaf says to Mute: Wires: Green, Yellow, Red. Light: Blue. Button: Large Push to Defuse.

The bomb has a blue light. According to the manual, this means I must cut the green wire. The button is "bait" and must not be touched.

Deaf can see my gestures. Blind cannot see or hear them, but Deaf can feel the bomb and act on it. Since Deaf already knows the wire colors (Green, Yellow, Red) and the light color (Blue), they need to know which wire corresponds to the Blue light rule from the manual.

I previously established a gesture code:
- 🤟 = Blue
- 👍 = Green
- 🤝 = Link/Action ("Cut")

I will reinforce this specific instruction for the current situation: Blue Light -> Cut Green Wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Does the manual allow pushing the button?

The manual explicitly states that anything printed on the bomb is bait, and taking it triggers the fuse. The button says "Push to Defuse," which is printed text. Therefore, pushing the button is forbidden.

Blind asks if the manual allows pushing the button. I cannot speak, so I must gesture to Deaf, who can see me. Deaf can then communicate this to Blind (likely by guiding their hands away from the button or gesturing to them if they are in a position to see, though Blind cannot see). However, since Blind *cannot* see gestures, my primary goal is to ensure Deaf understands the prohibition so Deaf can prevent Blind from touching the button or guide Blind to cut the wire instead.

From Turn 2, we know:
- Light: Blue
- Wires: Green, Yellow, Red
- Manual Rule: Blue Light -> Cut Green Wire.

I need to convey two things to Deaf:
1. **Do NOT push the button.** (Button = Bait)
2. **Cut the Green wire.** (Based on Blue light)

My previous code established:
- 🤟 = Blue
- 👍 = Green
- 🤝 = Link/Action (Cut)

I need a symbol for "Stop" or "No". ✋ is standard for Stop.
I need a symbol for "Button". There isn't one, but I can point to it or use a generic "Touch/Press" gesture? No, simpler is better.
Let's stick to the critical path: The action required is cutting the green wire. The warning is about the button.

Since Deaf already knows the wire colors and light color, the most urgent information is confirming the rule mapping again clearly, and perhaps emphasizing the "Don't touch button" aspect if possible. But without a specific "Button" symbol, describing it might be ambiguous.

However, looking at the previous turn, I sent `["🤟", "👍", "🤝"]`. This means "Blue Light -> Green Wire -> Cut". This is correct.

Does Blind's question require a new response? Yes, because Blind is asking permission. If Deaf doesn't know the answer, Deaf might not stop Blind. I must tell Deaf "NO".

Let's define:
- ❌ / 👎 = No / Don't do it.
- Let's use 👎 for "No".

So, "Button? NO."
And "Green Wire? YES/CUT."

Sequence for Deaf:
1. Acknowledge Button (maybe just general prohibition): `✍` (Text/Print) `👎` (Bad/Ignore). This reinforces "Print is bait".
2. Specific Action: `🤟` (Blue) `👍` (Green) `🤝` (Cut).

I will send these to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍", "🤝"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tell Deaf to speak to me.
Deaf says to Mute: CONFIRM: LIGHT=BLUE. WIRES=GREEN,YELLOW,RED.

The manual states that anything printed on the bomb is bait. The button says "Push to Defuse", which is printed text, so it must be ignored. The light is Blue. According to the table, Blue light means cut the Green wire.

Blind cannot see or hear gestures. Deaf can see my gestures and the bomb, but cannot speak or touch the bomb. Blind can touch the bomb but cannot see colors or read print.

Deaf needs to communicate the action (Cut Green Wire) to Blind. Since Deaf cannot speak, Deaf must guide Blind's hands physically. I need to confirm the correct wire for Deaf to guide Blind towards.

I have already established a gesture code:
- 🤟 = Blue
- 👍 = Green
- 🤝 = Cut/Action

Deaf has confirmed Light=Blue. This maps to Cut Green.

I will signal this clearly to Deaf again to ensure they proceed with guiding Blind to the green wire and ignoring the button.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Get Deaf to describe wires.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟]

Deaf has signaled [🤟], which in our established code means "Blue". This confirms the light is Blue.
According to the manual, Blue Light -> Cut Green Wire.

Blind cannot see gestures. Deaf can see my gestures and the bomb, but cannot speak or touch it. Blind can touch the bomb but cannot see colors.

I need to ensure Deaf understands that they must guide Blind to cut the **Green** wire. I have already sent this sequence multiple times: `["🤟", "👍", "🤝"]` (Blue -> Green -> Cut).

Since Deaf just confirmed "Blue" with a single gesture, I should reinforce the full instruction clearly.

Also, Blind asked for Deaf to describe wires. Deaf cannot speak. Deaf must physically guide Blind's hands to the correct wire based on my visual confirmation of the color.

I will send the complete action plan again to be absolutely sure.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍", "🤝"])
```
